Sync between two phones (tap to expand)

Do this once to pair. Tap "Copy my data", send it to your person, and have them paste it into Import on their phone. This gives you both the same secret, which is what makes your daily codes line up. After that, re-sync whenever you want to share progress.

Apple Health sync. Paste the link of your shared health Gist once (the setup guide explains how to create it and the iPhone Shortcuts that feed it). Steps, calories and sleep then show for both of you on the Health card.

Auto-sync (recommended). With the Gist link above plus your GitHub token here, both phones share everything automatically — tasks, trips, points, spins. The token stays on this phone only; paste the same one on both phones. It's the same token from the Health setup guide.

Push notifications. Get notified when your person adds or finishes something. This needs a free OneSignal account — the five steps are below. Paste the App ID (safe to share) and REST API key (stays on this phone, same trust level as your GitHub token above), then tap Enable on each phone.

How to get the two keys (about 5 minutes, once)
  1. Go to onesignal.com and make a free account.
  2. New App/Website → name it WeDO → platform Web.
  3. Choose Typical Site. Site URL: https://moodyjones.github.io/Us/ — it must match exactly, including the trailing slash. Leave "My site is not fully HTTPS" unticked.
  4. Skip the code step: WeDO already ships the SDK and the worker file.
  5. Settings → Keys & IDs. Copy the App ID and the REST API Key into the two boxes below, tap Save, then Enable on this phone. Do the same on the other phone.

iPhone will not deliver push to a Safari tab. WeDO has to be opened from the Home Screen icon. Permission belongs to that installed copy, not to Safari — each icon is its own small app with its own permission.

Updating WeDO does not break this. The icon points at an address, so a new version just loads. You never have to re-add it because the app changed.

There are only three reasons to delete the icon and add it again: you tapped Don't Allow at some point (iOS will not ask twice for the same installed copy); you added it with Open as Web App turned off, which makes a plain bookmark that push cannot reach; or you added it from an address other than moodyjones.github.io/Us/. Re-adding wipes that copy's WeDO data, so let it sync first.

Not working after that? Use Something looks off? at the bottom of this panel — it names the exact step that is failing.

Something looks off? Run this on BOTH phones and compare — it checks the build, sync setup, connections, and trip images, and says exactly what's wrong.

Living together? The daily code trade exists to make you actually talk when you're apart. Under one roof it's busywork — and missing it locks the app the next morning. Turn this on and the codes, the lock and the check-in card all go away. This one is shared: it changes for both of you.

Phone owner. Not set yet. Daily codes only show on their owner's phone. Only change this if it's genuinely wrong.

Lists look empty or wrong? This wipes this phone's data and reloads the starter lists (IKEA list, M&R to-dos, and the RÖoDaY bucket list with your 4 trophies).

What WeDO counts. It records which features get used — that a task was completed, that a photo was posted, which screen you opened. It never sends what you write, photograph or tick off: no task titles, no notes, no photos, no names.

Tell us what's broken. This sends exactly what you type here and nothing else from the app.

Device PIN. Locks this app on this phone so someone picking it up can't read your lists. It does not protect the web address itself — treat the URL as the real secret and don't share it.
